questions.q: What does cardinality describe about a relationship?
options: Whether values can repeat on each side of the relationship
Which table loads first
How many columns each table has
Whether the relationship is active or inactive
questions.explain: Cardinality answers whether a value can appear more than once on each side — for example, one dimension row matching many fact rows.

questions.q: Which cardinality is the default, most common shape for a fact table pointing at a dimension table?
options: Many to one (*:1)
One to one (1:1)
Many to many (*:*)
There is no default — you must always set it manually
questions.explain: Many to one is the typical shape: many fact rows referencing one dimension row. Power BI sets this automatically for most relationships.

questions.q: When does Power BI automatically set a relationship's cardinality to one to one?
options: When it detects that values never repeat on either side of the relationship
Whenever two tables have the same number of rows
Only when you manually request it
Never — one to one must always be set by hand
questions.explain: If both columns in a relationship happen to hold unique values, Power BI recognizes the one-to-one shape and configures it automatically.

questions.q: Why might you override an automatically-set one-to-one cardinality to many-to-one instead?
options: Because you know future data refreshes will introduce duplicate values on one side
Because many-to-one relationships load faster in every case
One-to-one relationships are always invalid in Power BI
To disable query folding
questions.explain: A one-to-one relationship breaks the moment duplicates appear on either side. If you know that's coming, setting many-to-one ahead of time avoids that break.

questions.q: Why does cardinality matter beyond just labeling a relationship?
options: It determines which side of the relationship can be correctly summarized and grouped by the other
It only affects how the relationship line is drawn in Model view
It has no effect on how Power BI calculates results
It controls which theme colors a visual uses
questions.explain: Cardinality isn't cosmetic — the 'many' side is what gets summed and grouped by its related 'one' side. Getting it backwards produces wrong or blocked results.
